reason: S1 adds the public blocking API ares_queue_wait_empty and a new condition-variable protocol tied to channel queue state, threading support, timeout_ms, query completion, cancellation, and destruction. H0 only invokes ares_create_query and stateless ares_parse_*_reply functions; it neither creates an ares_channel_t nor controls pending queries, threading configuration, timeouts, callbacks, cancellation, or destruction. Therefore H0 cannot reach or meaningfully exercise the newly introduced API and its state transitions, and this gap did not exist in S0 because the entry point and protocol were absent.
evidence: include/ares.h newly declares CARES_EXTERN ares_status_t ares_queue_wait_empty(ares_channel_t *channel, int timeout_ms).
ares_queue_wait_empty branches on ares_threadsafety(), channel == NULL, timeout_ms < 0, ares__llist_len(channel->all_queries), and timed versus indefinite condition waits.
ares__channel_threading_init newly creates channel->cond_empty, while ares__channel_threading_destroy destroys it.
ares_queue_notify_empty broadcasts channel->cond_empty only when channel->all_queries is empty and is newly called from ares_cancel, ares_destroy, and end_query.
test/ares-test-fuzz-name.c only calls ares_create_query with fixed class, type, ID, flags, and maximum size.
test/ares-test-fuzz.c only passes input bytes to ares_parse_*_reply functions and does not initialize or operate an ares_channel_t.
The S0 declaration context explicitly contains no matching declaration, whereas S1 contains ares_queue_wait_empty.
recommended_action: Add a stateful harness that initializes an ares_channel_t under supported threading configurations, creates controllable pending-query states, and exercises ares_queue_wait_empty with zero, finite, and negative timeouts across completion, callback-enqueued work, ares_cancel, and safe destruction paths.
